name: Tufte CSS (translated)
description: Tufte CSS's long-form book look on the t-* vocabulary: et-book/Palatino serif, generous leading, weight-400 italic headings, hairline rules instead of boxes, no fills, no shadows, 2px corners. App components Tufte never had (buttons, forms, badges, toasts, dialogs, switches) are printed labels: thin tone-coloured rules and italics, never loud fills.
notes: Translated, not vendored: tufte.css styles bare elements page-wide (body width/padding, 15px root, 1.4rem paragraphs, 55 % measure, sidenote counters) and has no controls, tables cells, nav or dialog, so nothing can be aliased onto tailor markup. Fonts: the stack leads with the et-book family names (et-book, 'ET Book') and falls back to Palatino / Palatino Linotype / Book Antiqua / Georgia / serif; the et-book woff files (MIT) are NOT shipped here — a project wanting the real face adds the four @font-face rules itself. Links inherit the ink and are underlined (Tufte); --t-link appears only on hover. Semantic tones stay distinguishable as tone-coloured hairlines/text, never washes. Dark palettes read as Tufte's own dark mode (colour-only swap).
